## Abstract

Objective: This study aimed to investigate the diagnostic performance of CT myocardial perfusion imaging (CT-MPI)  in detecting myocardial ischemia in patients with intermediate coronary stenosis

(50%–70%) using fractional flow reserve (FFR) as the reference standards.

Methods: Consecutive patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) diagnosed using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were prospectively enrolled and scanned with adenosine-

stress dynamic CT-MPI and referred to invasive coronary angiography (ICA) and FFR within 10 days. The inclusion criteria were as follows: intermediate coronary artery stenosis confirmed using quantitative ICA,

and the FFR was measured to assess its hemodynamic significance.

Results: In 31 patients, intermediate stenosis was confirmed using ICA in 31 vessels, and FFR was

measured in these vessels. Based on the FFR results, 24 vessels were assessed as causing ischemia in 24 patients (FFR £ 0.80). On a per-vessel basis, the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive values (PPV)

and negative predictive values (NPV) and diagnostic accuracy of absolute myocardial blood flow (MBF) and relative MBF were 79.17%, 85.71%, 54.54%, 95%, and 80.65% and 95.83%, 85.71%, 85.71%, 95.83%,

and 93.55%, respectively. With FFR £ 0.8 as a positive event, the area under the curve (AUC) values for the qualitative (visual) assessment, absolute MBF, and relative MBF were found to be 0.601, 0.792, and

0.899, respectively. The relative MBF was higher than the qualitative assessment (P < 0.05). The AUC of the relative MBF value was higher than the absolute MBF value, but the difference was not statistically

significant (P = 0.0649). The absolute MBF cutoff value was 116.275 mL·100 mL-1·min-1, and the relative MBF cutoff value was 0.736.

Conclusion: The CT-MPI is feasible in detecting myocardial ischemia in patients with intermediate

coronary stenosis.

## Key Points

1. In patients with intermediate coronary artery disease (CAD), adenosine-stress dynamic CT-MPI can

reflect hemodynamic changes as confirmed using invasive FFR.

2. The area under the ROC curve of relative MBF in diagnosing the hemodynamic changes of

intermediate CAD was higher than that in qualitative assessment; however, it was only slightly higher

than that of the absolute MBF with no statistical difference. 3. For patients with intermediate CAD, the optimal cutoff values of the absolute and relative MBF for

hemodynamic changes were 116.275 ml·100 ml− 1·min− 1 and 0.736, respectively.

## Introduction

It is crucial to determine whether coronary artery disease (CAD) leads to myocardial ischemia for clinical decision-making processes. However, there is no linear relationship between the degree of vascular stenosis and the severity of myocardial ischemia, and there is uncertainty regarding whether intermediate


<!-- Page 4 -->


Page 4/17

CAD (50–70%) leads to myocardial ischemia1. Previous studies have reported that approximately onethird of patients with intermediate CAD have myocardial ischemia [1, 2]. Therefore, functional assessment of patients with intermediate CAD has important clinical implications for optimizing

revascularization strategies [3].

Currently, fractional flow reserve (FFR) is the gold standard for evaluating the hemodynamic significance of intermediate CAD, and it is also used as a guide to determine if revascularization should be performed. Recently, the guidelines for coronary intervention in Europe, USA, and China have listed FFR-guided

coronary revascularization as a class IA recommendation; however, the invasiveness and high cost of FFR examination render the application of this diagnostic technique difficult to popularize. Over the past decade, with the continuous development of CT technology, dynamic CT myocardial perfusion imaging (CT-MPI) has become a promising noninvasive method for evaluating hemodynamic changes in CAD [4–

6]. However, the application of stress dynamic CT-MPI in patients with intermediate CAD has not yet been elucidated. In this study, invasive coronary angiography (ICA) and FFR were used as reference standards to investigate the ability of stress dynamic CT-MPI to determine the hemodynamic significance of intermediate CAD as well as to preliminarily explore its quantitative indicators and cutoff values of

myocardial perfusion.

## Materials and Methods

## Patients

The study prospectively and consecutively enrolled patients with clinically suspected CAD who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), stress dynamic CT-MPI, ICA, and FFR within a period of 10 days from April 2019 to December 2021. Patients with intermediate CAD as confirmed using

quantitative ICA analysis who also underwent FFR were included in this study. The exclusion criteria were as follows: (1) poor quality of stress dynamic CT-MPI images; (2) history of coronary revascularization; (3) history of myocardial infarction; and (4) patients with suspected cardiomyopathy or microcirculatory dysfunction. This study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian

Medical University (PJ-XJS-2019-79). Patients and their families signed informed consent forms.

## CCTA and stress dynamic CT-MPI

## Preparation before the examination

Patients were fully rested and caffeine-containing drugs, beverages (tea, coffee), food, and betaadrenergic blockers were prohibited for 24 h before the examination. Patients were provided breath-


<!-- Page 6 -->


Page 6/17

holding training before CCTA and stress dynamic CT-MPI examinations. Two venous accesses (indwelling catheters in the antecubital vein) were established for injecting iodinated contrast medium

and adenosine. Acquisition methods for CCTA and stress dynamic CT-MPI

A third-generation dual-source CT (Somatom Force, Siemens Healthineers, Forchheim, Germany) was used. The interval time between CCTA and stress dynamic CT-MPI was > 60 min. CCTA

A prospective ECG-triggered sequence scanning mode was used with a gantry rotation speed of 0.25

s/revolution, detector alignment of 2 × 96 × 0.6 mm, slice thickness of 0.75 mm, and slice interval of 0.7

mm.

Iodine contrast agent injection scheme: The iodine contrast agent automatic tracking technology was used, the region of interest was set in the ascending aorta or aortic arch, and the iodine contrast agent (iohexol 300 mg I/ml, Yangzijiang Pharmaceuticals) was injected through the anterior cubital vein using a

high pressure syringe. After the CT value of the region of interest exceeded the set threshold, the CCTA scan was started after a delay of 4 s. The iodine contrast medium was injected in three phases. In the first and second phases, 40–50 ml and 20–30 ml of iodine contrast medium was injected at a flow rate of 5.5–6 ml/s and 3.5–4.0 ml/s, respectively. In the third phase, 30 ml of normal saline was injected at a

flow rate of 4.0 ml/s. Stress dynamic CT-MPI

A coronary calcium integral CT scan was performed, and the prospective ECG-triggered scan mode with a slice thickness of 3 mm was adopted. The stress dynamic CT-MPI scan range (covering the entire left ventricular myocardium) was set with reference to cardiac CT cross-sectional images obtained using the

coronary calcium integral CT scan. Adenosine (Penglai Nuokang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.) was injected through a microinjection pump at a flow rate of 0.14 mg/kg/min for 3 min. Then, 56 ml of iodine contrast medium (iohexol 300 mg I/s, Yangzijiang Pharmaceutical) was injected at a flow rate of 7 ml/s using a high pressure syringe. Stress dynamic CT-MPI scanning and acquisition began 4 s after the start of iodine contrast agent injection, and 20 ml of normal saline was added after the injection. Moreover, prospective ECG-triggered shuttle scan mode with a tube voltage of 70 kV and automatic tube current adjustment technique (CARE Dose 4D) with a gantry rotation speed of 0.25 s/rev and detector alignment of 2 × 96 ×

0.6 mm were used for dynamic acquisition in the end-systole phase (250 ms after ECG R wave). Furthermore, the slice thickness was 3 mm, layer spacing was 2 mm, and scanning time was 32 s. The adenosine injection was stopped immediately after the CT scan, and the patient was asked about symptoms and was further assessed. The patient’s heart rate was continuously monitored during the stress dynamic CT-MPI. Image reconstruction and post-processing of CCTA and dynamic CT-MPI


<!-- Page 7 -->


Page 7/17

A smoothing convolution kernel (Bv 40) and the third-generation iterative reconstruction technology (strength 3, ADMIRE, Siemens) were used for the cross-sectional CT image reconstruction of CCTA, and the image data were transferred to an offline workstation (SyngoViaVB10, Siemens Healthineers, Forchheim, Germany). Subsequently, two-dimensional surface reconstruction and maximum density projection reconstruction were performed on three coronary arteries (left anterior descending, left circumflex, and right coronary arteries).

A convolution kernel (Qr36) was adopted for image reconstruction of dynamic CT-MPI. The myocardial perfusion post-processing software (Volume Perfusion CT Body) was used to post-process the images and generate pseudocolor images (short-axis two-chamber and long-axis two- and four-chamber images). The manual correction was performed in cases where the automatic identification of the cardiac chambers was inaccurate. Moreover, myocardial blood flow (MBF) was quantified using the arterial input function to measure iodinated contrast influx. Image assessment of stress dynamic CT-MPI

The images were assessed using a double-blind method. Two physicians (with 6 and 8 years of work experience in cardiac CT diagnosis) performed the diagnostic evaluation of stress dynamic CT-MPI images. When the results were inconsistent, a third physician (with 15 years of experience in cardiac CT

diagnosis) provided the final judgment. Qualitative assessment was performed as follows: the presence or absence of myocardial perfusion defect was visually assessed based on the reconstructed threedimensional pseudocolor image of the heart. Perfusion defects were defined as hypoperfusion areas in two or more consecutive layers at the same position. Quantitative assessment was performed as follows: MBF (also known as absolute MBF) and MBF ratio (also known as relative MBF) were measured and calculated. Based on the bull’s eye image of the CT-MPI, a region of interest (ROI) was drawn in each myocardial segment. When drawing the ROI, the entire segment should be included and the junction between the endocardium and epicardium should be avoided as much as possible. The absolute MBF of

the apical segment and the other 16 segments was measured on the vertical long-axis and short-axis images, respectively, and the relative MBF was calculated by two physicians who measured and averaged them separately (relative MBF = lesioned segment MBF/reference segment MBF). The 17-segment myocardium was divided into three regions: left anterior descending artery (segments 1, 2, 7, 8, 13, 14, and 17), left circumflex artery (segments 3, 4, 9, 10, and 15), and right coronary artery (segments 5, 6, 11, 12, and 16) supply areas [7]. The reference segment was defined as the segment with the highest absolute MBF among the 17 segments, whereas the lesioned segment was defined as the segment with the lowest absolute MBF in the myocardial segment dominated by borderline lesion. The effective radiation dose

The CT dose index volume of CCTA and dose length product (DLP) of stress dynamic CT-MPI were recorded, and the effective radiation dose was calculated according to the following formula: Effective

radiation dose (mSv) = DLP × k (adult conversion factor k = 0.014 mSv·mGy− 1·cm− 1). Examination and diagnostic criteria of the ICA and FFR

## ICA

Using a flat-panel fully digital angiography machine (Innova IGS 520, General Electric, USA), a 5F coronary angiography catheter was inserted through a radial or femoral artery puncture to perform selective right coronary angiography and left coronary angiography sequentially. The iodine contrast medium used for this examination was the nonionic iodine contrast agent iodixanol (Iodixanol, 320 mg I/ml, General Electric, USA). Image acquisition (cine mode) for the left and right coronary angiography was performed in 4–6 and 2–3 body positions, respectively.

The ICA images were read and quantitatively analyzed by two cardiovascular radiologists (with more than 5 years of clinical work experience), and any inconsistencies were resolved through consultation. The degree of CAD was based on the average value of the relative normal lumen diameter at the proximal and distal sides of the stenosis and was expressed as the percentage reduction in the lumen diameter of the stenosis. Intermediate CAD was defined as 50–70% stenosis. FFR

For the intermediate CAD indicated by ICA, the myocardium was induced to reach a maximal hyperemia state via intravenous infusion of the stress drug adenosine (0.14 mg/kg/min). The FFR of intermediate CAD was measured using a pressure guide wire under adenosine-induced hyperemia via the QuantienTM Pressure WireTM interface. An FFR value of ≤ 0.80 was considered hemodynamically significant for vessel stenosis. Statistical analysis

Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS 22.0 and the Medcalc software. Histograms were created to confirm whether the measured data conformed to the normal distribution. Data conforming to the normal distribution were expressed as x ± s, whereas data that did not conform to the normal distribution were expressed as the median and interquartile range. Continuous variables with the normal distribution were compared using an independent sample t test, whereas continuous variables without the normal

distribution were compared using t′ test. Interobserver agreement was assessed using ICC. The ROC curve was drawn, and the area under the curve (AUC) was calculated and compared using the DeLong test to assess the diagnostic power. The diagnostic cutoff value was quantitatively assessed using the Youden index, and the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive values and negative predictive values (PPV and NPV), and diagnostic accuracy were calculated based on the statistical methods of diagnostic tests. A P value of < 0.05 was considered as statistically significant.

## Results

## Study population and distribution of coronary borderline lesions


<!-- Page 9 -->


Page 9/17

Thirty-one patients with intermediate CAD (31 intermediate stenotic coronary vessels), comprising 25 males and six females with an average age of 59.12 ± 8.11 years, were included in this study. The patients’ average heart rate increment after adenosine stress was 17.27 ± 11.34 bmp. The DLP of these

patients with dynamic CT-MPI was 298.67 ± 118.51, and the effective radiation dose was 4.18 ± 1.66 mSv. Basic clinical data are shown in Table 1.

The intermediate CAD of 31 coronary arteries (21 for the left anterior descending artery, 4 for the left circumflex artery, and 6 for the right coronary artery) had a stenosis degree of 64.42% ± 7.15%. Twentyfour coronary arteries (17 for the left anterior descending artery, 4 for the left circumflex, and 3 for the right coronary artery) had an average FFR value of ≤ 0.80, whereas 7 arteries (4 for the left anterior descending artery and 3 for the right coronary artery) had an average FFR value of > 0.80. Among 24

coronary arteries of intermediate CAD with an FFR value of ≤ 0.80, 8 coronary arteries (5, 1, and 2 for the left anterior descending artery, left circumflex artery, and right coronary artery, respectively) had intermediate CAD with FFR values ranging from 0.75 to 0.80. Quantitative and qualitative assessment of intermediate CAD

The MBF of the myocardial segments dominated by intermediate CAD in 31 coronary arteries was

significantly lower than that of the reference segment (109.38 ± 23.22 ml·100 ml− 1·min− 1 vs. 171.12 ±

18.00 ml·100 ml− 1·min− 1; P < 0.001). The interobserver agreement for quantitative assessment was high (ICC value = 0.993). The MBF of the myocardial segment dominated by intermediate CAD in 24 coronary arteries with an FFR value of ≤ 0.80 was also significantly lower than that of the reference myocardial

segment (103.81 ± 20.79 ml·100 ml− 1·min− 1 vs. 172.97 ± 15.85 ml·100 ml− 1·min− 1; P < 0.001).

Of the 31 patients with intermediate CAD, 27 were diagnosed with myocardial perfusion defect via a qualitative evaluation (Figs. 2 and 3); of these, 5 were false-positive diagnoses. Four patients without myocardial perfusion defects were diagnosed via a qualitative assessment; of these, two were falsenegative diagnoses. The interobserver agreement of quantitative assessment was high (ICC value = 0.992). The value of CT-MPI in evaluating hemodynamic changes in borderline lesions

Considering an FFR value of ≤ 0.80 as a positive event, the ROC curves of qualitative assessment, absolute MBF, and relative MBF detection of critical CAD with hemodynamic significance were constructed. The AUC values for qualitative assessment, absolute MBF, and relative MBF were 0.601, 0.792, and 0.899, respectively (Fig. 1). The diagnostic performance of the relative MBF was better than that of the qualitative assessment (P < 0.05). Moreover, the diagnostic performance of the relative MBF was insignificantly better than that of the absolute MBF (P = 0.0649), and the diagnostic performance of the absolute MBF was insignificantly better than that of the qualitative assessment (P = 0.0759). In

addition, the optimal cutoff values of the absolute and relative MBF were 116.275 ml·100 ml− 1·min− 1


<!-- Page 10 -->


Page 10/17

and 0.736, respectively. Using FFR as the gold standard, the relative MBF had high sensitivity and PPV for

the diagnosis of hemodynamic changes in borderline lesions, with moderate-to-high specificity and NPV (Table 2).

Furthermore, myocardial perfusion defect was diagnosed in six of eight patients with intermediate CAD, with FFR values ranging from 0.75 to 0.80, using qualitative assessment, absolute MBF, and relative MBF.

## Discussion

In this study, 31 patients with intermediate CAD underwent adenosine-stress dynamic CT-MPI examination using a third-generation dual-source CT. The study found that using invasive FFR as the gold

standard and considering the blood vessel as the unit, the performance of relative MBF in diagnosing hemodynamic changes in intermediate CAD was better than that of qualitative assessment, with an AUC value of 0.899. When the best cutoff value for relative MBF was 0.736, the specificity and PPV were 85.71% and 95.83%, respectively, and the sensitivity and NPV were 95.83% and 85.71%, respectively.

Intermediate CAD is an intermediate state in the development of CAD, and the formulation of treatment strategies based solely on coronary anatomical stenosis usually leads to over- or undertreatment, resulting in poor prognosis [8]. Recently, the CAD-RADSTM guidelines clearly stated that when CCTA shows intermediate CAD, FFR should be performed to determine whether the lesion has hemodynamic

significance[9]; if the result is positive, coronary revascularization can reduce adverse cardiac outcomes. However, it is extremely difficult to use FFR in clinical settings. In this study, FFR was used as the gold standard. The results showed that the hemodynamic changes in intermediate CAD detected using stress dynamic CT-MPI had high sensitivity and PPV as well as moderate-to-high specificity and NPV. Moreover, a previous study has shown that stress dynamic CT-MPI has high sensitivity to hemodynamic changes caused by obstructive CAD, indicating that this method has clinical warning ability equivalent to that of FFR [10]. When stress dynamic CT-MPI is positive, revascularization of coronary lesions should be performed to avoid unnecessary FFR examinations and reduce the occurrence of adverse cardiovascular

events, thus indicating that this method can be used as a first-line treatment for patients with intermediate CAD.

Furthermore, this study showed that the diagnostic performance of relative MBF in dynamic CT-MPI based on adenosine stress was better than that of qualitative assessment, with AUC values of 0.899 and 0.601, respectively. However, it only showed a slight advantage (no statistical difference) compared with that of absolute MBF, which may be attributed to the small sample size used in this study. Nous et al. [6] used a third-generation dual-source CT to perform adenosine-stress dynamic CT-MPI in 74 patients with CAD. Considering the FFR value of ≤ 0.80 as the reference standard for the diagnosis of myocardial

ischemia, the results showed that there was no significant difference between relative MBF and absolute MBF in the diagnosis of myocardial ischemia (AUC values of 0.82 and 0.79, respectively). However, some other studies [11–14] have shown that the relative MBF index was better than qualitative assessment and absolute MBF, and this finding may be associated with congenital deficiencies in qualitative assessment and absolute MBF. Qualitative evaluation is inevitably affected by observer experience and subjective factors, such as artificial adjustment of window width and window level, whereas absolute MBF is easily affected by the types of loaded drugs, individual response differences, and different mathematical

calculation models. The threshold for absolute MBF varied greatly (75–103 ml·100 ml− 1·min− 1) in

several studies [15–20]. The absolute MBF threshold obtained in this study was 116.275 ml·100 ml−

1·min− 1, which was higher than that reported in previous studies. In addition to the influence of the above individual differences, the main reason for this might be that we only included patients with intermediate


<!-- Page 12 -->


Page 12/17

CAD (average degree of stenosis, 64.42%), in which the degree of stenosis was smaller than that reported in previous studies. Consequently, myocardial perfusion consistently increased in this study. Relative MBF uses normal segmental myocardium for intraindividual correction, which can reduce interindividual differences to a certain extent. Thus, relative MBF may truly reflect the hemodynamic changes caused by intermediate CAD and has greater clinical application value. This study showed that when the optimal

cutoff value of relative MBF was 0.736, stress dynamic CT-MPI showed the best diagnostic performance for hemodynamic changes in intermediate CAD. In addition, the relative MBF threshold obtained in this study was higher than that reported by Yi et al. (0.675) [12]. The reason might be similar to the one stated for the absolute MBF threshold. However, due to different calculation formulas, the relative MBF thresholds reported in the literature were also different (0.675–0.75) [12, 14, 21]. A multi-center clinical study with a large sample size should be conducted in the future to unify the calculation formula and

establish an effective threshold. So far, only the study conducted by Yi et al [22]. has shown that the diagnostic performance of absolute MBF was better than that of relative MBF, which might be attributed

to the inclusion of more patients with multivessel CAD in their study. Overall, compared with absolute MBF, the relative MBF cutoff values did not vary significantly across studies, indicating that it is a more

reliable indicator of myocardial perfusion.

Another interesting finding of this study was that the FFR of eight patients was in the controversial gray

area (0.75–0.80); of these, six had a clear diagnosis of myocardial ischemia via qualitative assessment

and quantitative indicators on stress dynamic CT-MPI, suggesting that stress dynamic CT-MPI might reflect the development of CAD earlier than FFR. Considering this viewpoint, stress dynamic CT-MPI may

play a complementary role in clinical decision-making of patients in the gray area of FFR. Both stress dynamic CT-MPI and FFR are functional examination methods for CAD. FFR refers to the ratio of the

maximum blood flow that can be obtained in the myocardial region supplied by the coronary artery in the presence of stenotic lesions and the maximum blood flow that can be obtained in the same region

without stenotic lesions [23]. Stress dynamic CT-MPI is a noninvasive imaging method for evaluating

myocardial blood perfusion, which can provide information on the extent and degree of myocardial ischemia to determine the hemodynamic significance of the corresponding diseased vessels. Differences

in the imaging principles between the two methods may be the reason why they complement each other in controversial cases.

Currently, due to the high technical requirements of the CT scanner, high radiation dose, interference of beam hardening artifacts, and cardiac motion artifacts, individual differences in the efficacy of stress

drugs, and lack of standard of perfusion quantitative indicators for the diagnosis of myocardial ischemia, popularization and application of this technology is restricted to a certain extent. The radiation dose of

stress dynamic CT-MPI in our study was 4.18 ± 1.66 mSv. Overall, the radiation dose of this examination

is still high compared with that of the widely used CCTA in clinical practice. It is believed that with the advancement of CT software and hardware technology and the development of related stress drugs,

stress dynamic CT-MPI will definitely become a common noninvasive examination method for evaluating the hemodynamic changes in CAD.

Page 13/17

Our study has several limitations. First, this was a single-center study with a small sample size. Second,

although all enrolled patients had intermediate CAD, the average degree of stenosis was still high and the proportion of patients with hemodynamic significance was relatively large, which could have a certain

bias. Third, all patients were scanned using third-generation dual-source CT scans, and MBF was calculated using the hybrid deconvolution method and the maximum slope model. Therefore, it is

necessary to conduct further multi-center, multi-model studies with a large sample size to verify and explore the clinical significance and applicability of our findings.

In conclusion, dynamic CT-MPI with adenosine stress can assess the hemodynamic significance of

critical CAD with high sensitivity and PPV as well as moderate-to-high specificity and NPV. Among the three indicators, relative MBF may be a more valuable indicator for detecting myocardial ischemia;

however, it needs to be further verified via multi-center studies with a large sample size.
